subject.title: [Feature]: Add before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes, or should durable-write policy be represented through enriched before_tool_call/provenance contracts instead?
rationale: This choice defines a public Plugin SDK security boundary over persisted user and agent state, including what data plugins can see, whether they can block or mutate writes, and how hook failures affect durable state.

options.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow before_persistence_write contract with redacted targets, explicit block or mutation rules, bounded failure policy, docs, and writer-path tests after maintainer/security review.

options.title: Fold durable context into existing policy hooks
options.body: Extend before_tool_call and related provenance/read-time APIs instead of adding a new hook family, reducing hook count but requiring broader taxonomy work first.

options.title: Defer to provenance architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open as a dependency of the broader persistent-state provenance work until maintainers settle the end-to-end trust model.

recommendation.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow before_persistence_write contract with redacted targets, explicit block or mutation rules, bounded failure policy, docs, and writer-path tests after maintainer/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: The current hook and writer surfaces route most clearly through vincentkoc's recent merged history, and the issue references adjacent operator-policy security work.
